label: lem:green-transform
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:transformed-transition
title: Proof
body_md:
The function $h$ is positive, equals one at $o$, and is harmonic
off $o$. For $x\ne o$, the transition probabilities of the
transformed network satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \widehat P(x,y)=P(x,y)\frac{h(y)}{h(x)}\qquad(y\sim x).
 \label{eq:transformed-transition}
\end{equation}
Up to its first visit to $o$, this is the original walk conditioned
to hit $o$. Every departure from $o$ therefore returns almost surely,
which proves recurrence.

Fix an edge from $p=x^-$ to $x$. The voltage
formula and the Green function killed on hitting $p$ give
\begin{equation}
 H(x,p)=\frac{c_{px}}{c_{px}+C_x^+}=\frac{h(x)}{h(p)},\qquad
 g(x,x)-\frac{g(p,x)^2}{g(p,p)}=\frac1{c_{px}+C_x^+}.
 \label{eq:edge-hitting-green}
\end{equation}
Both identities in \eqref{eq:edge-hitting-green} follow by finite
network exhaustion, including when $C_x^+=0$. Since
$g(p,x)=H(x,p)g(p,p)$, division yields
\begin{equation}
 \frac{g(x,x)}{h(x)^2}-\frac{g(p,p)}{h(p)^2}
 =\frac1{c_{px}h(p)h(x)}=\frac1{\widehat c_{px}}.
 \label{eq:green-increment}
\end{equation}
Summing \eqref{eq:green-increment} along $[o,x]$ and using
$g(x,x)/h(x)^2=g_o\rho_o(x)^{-2}$ proves
\eqref{eq:green-resistance}.
Every infinite ray has infinite total resistance in a recurrent
network: otherwise the unit flow supported on that ray would have
finite energy, contradicting the electrical transience criterion
\cite[Theorem~2.11]{LP}.
Equation~\eqref{eq:green-resistance} therefore gives
\eqref{eq:ray-correlation-decay}.

label: lem:branching
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:CIR-LT
title: Proof
body_md:
For $0<q\le1$, let $Q_q(z,\cdot)$ be the transition law of
\eqref{eq:CIR} after time $-\log q$, started at $z\ge0$, and write
$Q_qf(z)=\int f(y)Q_q(z,dy)$. Its Laplace transform is
\begin{equation}
 Q_q(e^{-\lambda\,\cdot})(z)
 =[1+(1-q)\lambda]^{-\alpha}
   \exp\left\{-\frac{qz\lambda}{1+(1-q)\lambda}\right\},\qquad\lambda\ge0.
 \label{eq:CIR-LT}
\end{equation}
Indeed, if $Y$ solves the stochastic differential equation
\begin{equation}
 dY_s=\sqrt{2Y_s}\,dB_s+\alpha\,ds,
 \label{eq:BESQ}
\end{equation}
driven by a standard Brownian motion, then $2Y$ is a squared-Bessel
process of dimension $2\alpha$ and the time change
\begin{equation}
 X_t=e^{-t}Y_{e^t-1}
 \label{eq:bessel-time-change}
\end{equation}
solves \eqref{eq:CIR} in law, with the same initial value.
Formula~\eqref{eq:CIR-LT} follows from the squared-Bessel
transition transform; see~\cite[Sections~4.1--4.2]{Lupu18}.
Integration against $\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha,1)$ shows that this law is invariant.

Fix finitely many points, including $a$. Their spanning tree is
the union of the geodesics joining these points, and we add its branch
points to the finite set. By \eqref{eq:multiplicative}, the normalized
Green matrix $R$ on this enlarged finite set has entries given by
products of correlations across the edges of its spanning tree.
Starting at $a$ with law $\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha,1)$, use the kernels $Q_q$
independently on the branches, where $q$ is the squared correlation
across an edge. We verify that the resulting field has transform
$\det(I+RD)^{-\alpha}$.

Let $l$ be a leaf with parent $p$, and put $q=R_{pl}^2$ and
$A=1+(1-q)\lambda_l$. Let $R_0$ and $D_0$ be the matrices
with the coordinate $l$ deleted, and let $e_p$ be the coordinate
vector at $p$ in the remaining space. By \eqref{eq:CIR-LT},
integrating out $X(l)$ multiplies the transform by $A^{-\alpha}$
and replaces $\lambda_p$ by $\lambda_p+q\lambda_l/A$. The same
recursion holds for the determinant: subtracting $\sqrt q$ times
row $p$ from row $l$ and eliminating the leaf coordinate gives
\begin{equation}
 \det(I+RD)
 =A\det\left(I+R_0\left[
        D_0+\frac{q\lambda_l}{A}e_pe_p^{\mathsf T}\right]\right).
 \label{eq:leaf}
\end{equation}
Induction in \eqref{eq:leaf} proves the transform identity, and
\eqref{eq:normalized-laplace} identifies the finite-dimensional laws.
Continuity on the cables then identifies the fields on countable
dense subsets, and hence their laws as continuous functions.
The independent construction on the branches proves the conditional
independence assertion.

label: prop:two-point
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:hit-zero
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:branching} and \eqref{eq:positive-path}, the
conditional connection probability is the probability that the
diffusion \eqref{eq:CIR}, started at $z$, avoids zero up to time
$-\log q$. By \eqref{eq:bessel-time-change}, this is the probability
that $Y$ avoids zero up to $(1-q)/q$. For $Y_0=z>0$, let
$T_0=\inf\{s\ge0:Y_s=0\}$. The squared-Bessel hitting-time formula gives
\begin{equation}
 T_0\overset d=\frac{z}{G_{1-\alpha}},
 \qquad G_{1-\alpha}\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(1-\alpha,1);
 \label{eq:hit-zero}
\end{equation}
see~\cite[Proposition~2.9]{LawlerBessel}, applied to $\sqrt{2Y}$
with Bessel parameter $\alpha-1/2$. This proves
\eqref{eq:conditional-connection}. For $z>0$, the derivative of
$F_{\alpha,q}$ is a positive constant times
$z^{-\alpha}e^{-zq/(1-q)}$, which is decreasing. Together with
$F_{\alpha,q}(0)=0$, this proves concavity.

Unconditionally, $X(u)\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha,1)$. Let
$G_\alpha\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(\alpha,1)$ be independent of $G_{1-\alpha}$ from
\eqref{eq:hit-zero}. Integrating \eqref{eq:conditional-connection} gives
\begin{equation}
 p_\alpha(u,v)
 =\mathbb P\left(G_{1-\alpha}<\frac{qG_\alpha}{1-q}\right)
 =\mathbb P\left(\frac{G_{1-\alpha}}{G_\alpha+G_{1-\alpha}}<q\right).
 \label{eq:gamma-ratio}
\end{equation}
The ratio in \eqref{eq:gamma-ratio} has the
$\operatorname{Beta}(1-\alpha,\alpha)$ law, which proves \eqref{eq:beta}.

In the beta integral, $(1-t)^{\alpha-1}\ge1$. For $q\le1/2$ it
is also at most $2^{1-\alpha}$ on $[0,q]$. For $q>1/2$, use
$I_q(1-\alpha,\alpha)\le1\le2^{1-\alpha}q^{1-\alpha}$. These estimates give
\eqref{eq:power}, with constants adjusted to include $u=v$.

If $\alpha\ge1$, the squared-Bessel process started above zero
never hits zero; see~\cite[Proposition~2.1]{LawlerBessel}.
Every neighboring pair of vertices is therefore connected almost
surely. There are countably many edges, and their connecting
geodesics cover $\widetilde T$. This proves \eqref{eq:full-connection}.

label: lem:concavity
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:size-biased-comparison
title: Proof
body_md:
For any $f=f_i$, concavity and nonnegativity at zero imply that $f(z)/z$ is
decreasing for $z>0$. Under the size-biased law
$dQ=Z\,d\mathbb P/\mathbb E Z$, it has nonpositive covariance with every
increasing function $\psi$ for which the terms are integrable.
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(Z)\psi(Z)]\le\frac{\mathbb E f(Z)}{\mathbb E Z}\mathbb E[Z\psi(Z)].
 \label{eq:size-biased-comparison}
\end{equation}
Apply \eqref{eq:size-biased-comparison} successively to
$f_1,\ldots,f_k$. At the $i$th step,
$\psi$ is a product of the remaining increasing nonnegative factors
and $Z^{i-1}$, so it is increasing. Gamma moments ensure
integrability. This yields \eqref{eq:concavity}.
head: environment

label: prop:quasi
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:three-connections
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $o,x,y$ lie in three different components of
$\widetilde T\setminus\{a\}$. For $v\in\{o,x,y\}$, set
$f_v(z)=F_{\alpha,\rho(a,v)^2}(z)$. Conditional on $Z=X(a)$,
the three events $\{a\leftrightarrow v\}$ are independent with
increasing concave probabilities $f_v(Z)$ by
\eqref{eq:conditional-connection}. Their simultaneous
occurrence is precisely the joint event in \eqref{eq:quasi}.
Equation~\eqref{eq:concavity}, with
$\mathbb E Z^3/(\mathbb E Z)^3=K_\alpha$, gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_\alpha^T(o\leftrightarrow x,\ o\leftrightarrow y)
 \le K_\alpha p_\alpha(o,a)p_\alpha(a,x)p_\alpha(a,y).
 \label{eq:three-connections}
\end{equation}
Two increasing functions of the same scalar variable have
nonnegative covariance. Therefore
\begin{equation}
 p(x)=\mathbb E[f_o(Z)f_x(Z)]
 \ge p_\alpha(o,a)p_\alpha(a,x),
 \label{eq:pair-positive-correlation}
\end{equation}
and the same inequality holds with $y$ in place of $x$. Substitution
in \eqref{eq:three-connections} proves \eqref{eq:quasi}. If $a=o$,
apply \eqref{eq:concavity} to $f_x$ and $f_y$; the moment constant
$(\alpha+1)/\alpha$ is at most $K_\alpha$.
If $a=x$ or $a=y$, the connection events are nested and the bound
holds with constant one.

label: lem:frostman
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:flow-correlation-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
The strict decrease of $\rho_o$ along paths and
\eqref{eq:ray-correlation-decay} show that $\delta_G$ is an
ultrametric. For a ray $\xi$ and $0<t<1$, the closed ball
$B_{\delta_G}(\xi,t)$ is $\partial T_{\xi_n}$, where $n$ is the first index
with $\rho_o(\xi_n)\le t$. Hence its topology is the cylinder
topology, which is compact by local finiteness.
If $s>D_G$, choose cutsets whose sums of $\rho_o(x)^s$ tend to
zero. Their cylinders cover $\partial T$ and have diameter at
most $\rho_o(x)$. The largest diameter also tends to zero, so the
$s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure is zero. If $D_G=0$, this already
proves \eqref{eq:green-boundary-dimension}.

Now fix $0<\beta<s<D_G$ and let $\delta$ be as in
\eqref{eq:frostman}.
Since $0<\rho_o(x)\le1$, the set of exponents with positive cutset
infimum is downward closed, so $\delta>0$. The max-flow/min-cut
theorem~\cite[Theorem~3.1]{LP}, with vertex capacities
$\rho_o(x)^s$, gives a unit flow satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mu(x)\le\delta^{-1}\rho_o(x)^s\qquad(x\in V).
 \label{eq:flow-correlation-bound}
\end{equation}
The description of balls above gives
$\mu(B_{\delta_G}(\xi,t))\le\delta^{-1}t^s$ for $0<t<1$.
Every set of positive diameter is contained in a closed ball of
that diameter, and singletons have zero mass by
\eqref{eq:ray-correlation-decay}. Thus every countable cover of
the boundary by sets of diameter less than one has sum of
$s$th powers of diameters at least $\delta$. This proves
$\dim_{\mathrm H}(\partial T,\delta_G)\ge s$, and establishes
\eqref{eq:green-boundary-dimension} by letting $s\uparrow D_G$.

For $\xi\in\partial T$, put $t_n=\rho_o(\xi_n)^{-\beta}$, so
$t_0=1$ and $t_n\uparrow\infty$ by \eqref{eq:ray-correlation-decay}.
Using \eqref{eq:flow-correlation-bound} in \eqref{eq:energy-series}
and applying Tonelli's theorem gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal E_\beta(\mu)-1
 &\le\delta^{-1}\sum_{x\ne o}\mu(x)\rho_o(x)^s
        [\rho_o(x)^{-\beta}-\rho_o(x^-)^{-\beta}]\\
 &=\delta^{-1}\int_{\partial T}
      \sum_{n\ge1}t_n^{-s/\beta}(t_n-t_{n-1})\,d\mu(\xi),
\end{aligned}
 \label{eq:energy-along-rays}
\end{equation}
where the sequence $(t_n)$ in the integral depends on $\xi$.
Since $t\mapsto t^{-s/\beta}$
is decreasing,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{n\ge1}t_n^{-s/\beta}(t_n-t_{n-1})
 \le\int_1^\infty t^{-s/\beta}\,dt=\frac{\beta}{s-\beta}.
 \label{eq:energy-integral-bound}
\end{equation}
Substituting \eqref{eq:energy-integral-bound} into
\eqref{eq:energy-along-rays} proves \eqref{eq:frostman}.
head: environment

label: eq:energy-two
title: Proof
body_md:
Definition~\eqref{eq:DG} gives $D_G\ge0$. To prove the upper bound, combine
\eqref{eq:green-resistance} and \eqref{eq:energy-series}:
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_2(\mu)
 =1+\frac1{g_o}\sum_{x\ne o}
              \frac{\mu(x)^2}{\widehat c_{x^-x}}.
 \label{eq:energy-two}
\end{equation}
If $D_G>2$, \eqref{eq:frostman} with $\beta=2$ would give
a finite-energy unit flow in the recurrent network
$(T,\widehat c)$, a contradiction. Thus $D_G\le2$.

For $0<\alpha<1$, put $\beta=2(1-\alpha)$.
If $\beta<D_G$, choose $\beta<s<D_G$ and apply
\eqref{eq:frostman} and \eqref{eq:survival} to get
positive probability of root percolation. If $\beta>D_G$, the
cutset infimum at exponent $\beta$ is zero, so
\eqref{eq:cutset-first-moment} and \eqref{eq:root-transfer} give
non-percolation.
Equation~\eqref{eq:full-connection} handles $D_G=0$ and all
intensities at least one. If $D_G=2$, the implication from
$\beta<D_G$ applies at every
$0<\alpha<1$. These statements prove \eqref{eq:classification}
throughout $0\le D_G\le2$.

The proof applies with any chosen root. Since the critical intensity
in \eqref{eq:critical} is defined without a root,
\eqref{eq:classification} proves that $D_G(T,o)$ is independent of $o$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:root-transfer}, applied in both directions, also
makes positive percolation probability equivalent at all fixed
vertices. Independence of the skeleton follows from
\eqref{eq:point-cutsets}.
head: environment

label: lem:point-cutsets
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Every vertex cutset is a point cutset, so the point infimum is no
larger. Conversely, start with a finite point cutset and discard
points belonging to no infinite ray. Move each point in the interior
of an edge to its endpoint farther from $o$. All rays previously
met are still met. By \eqref{eq:multiplicative}, each weight
$\rho_o(x)^s$ can only decrease. If necessary, discard duplicates
and descendants of other selected vertices so that no two remaining
vertices are ancestors of one another;
the remaining set still meets every ray. Thus the vertex infimum is
no larger than the point infimum. This proves
\eqref{eq:point-cutsets}. The left-hand side of
\eqref{eq:point-cutsets} uses only the metric tree and its Brownian
Green function. Both the length measure and the energy
\eqref{eq:brownian-energy} are unchanged when degree-two vertices
are inserted or removed. The exponent is therefore the same for
every weighted skeleton of this metric tree.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the skeleton theorem of
Athreya--Eckhoff--Winter~\cite[Lemma~7.1 and Remark~7.2]{AEW},
every point of $\mathcal T$ has finite degree, meaning that its removal
leaves finitely many connected components. Each bounded ball contains
only finitely many branch points, that is, points of degree at least
three. Include $o$ among these vertices
and insert degree-two vertices along any unbounded arcs. We obtain
a locally finite skeleton with finite positive edge lengths.

Assign conductance $c_e=(2\ell_e)^{-1}$ to an edge of length
$\ell_e$. The cable energy $\frac12\int|f'|^2$ is exactly the
Brownian energy on $\mathcal T$. For fixed values at the endpoints
$x,y$ of $e$, the least energy on that edge is
$c_e(f(x)-f(y))^2$, attained by linear interpolation.
Thus the cable diffusion, its Green
function and its loop soup agree with those on $\mathcal T$.
Equations~\eqref{eq:classification}, \eqref{eq:full-connection} and
\eqref{eq:point-cutsets} give \eqref{eq:real-tree-classification}
and full connection at intensity one.

label: eq:unit-ray-remainder
title: Proof
body_md:
Wire the finite path $[o,\xi_n]$ to one vertex, as in
Figure~\ref{fig:ray-capacity}. Its exterior
branches are disjoint and in parallel. The branches leaving before
$\xi_n$ contribute the sum in \eqref{eq:segment-capacity}, and
those leaving the endpoint contribute $C_{\xi_n}^+$. Requiring
potential one at the path vertices or on its whole cable gives the
same capacity, since the minimizing function is constant along
the intervening edges. This proves \eqref{eq:segment-capacity}.
Exhaustion gives the capacity of the full ray. Every unbounded
closed connected subset contains a ray tail, and a finite initial
segment has finite capacity, so this tests
\eqref{eq:capacity-condition}. In the unit case,
\begin{equation}
 C_{\xi_n}^+=s_n(\xi)+C_{\xi_n,\xi_{n+1}},\qquad
                         0\le C_{\xi_n,\xi_{n+1}}\le1.
 \label{eq:unit-ray-remainder}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eq:segment-capacity} and
\eqref{eq:unit-ray-remainder} proves the equivalence with
\eqref{eq:ray-capacity-condition}.
head: environment

label: lem:pruning
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Extend a finitely supported function on $T^\infty$ constantly over
every attached finite branch. Only finitely many attachment vertices
have nonzero values, and each has finitely many finite branches, so
the extension still has finite support. It adds zero energy.
Conversely, restriction from $T$ to $T^\infty$ cannot increase
energy. Thus minimizing the energy over extensions of a function
on $T^\infty$ gives exactly its energy in the pruned tree.
The variational characterizations
give transience, equality of Green functions and equality of
capacities. The same argument proves transience of $T$ whenever
$T^\infty$ is transient. This is the finite-branch reduction used
also in~\cite[Section~1, (1.31)--(1.40)]{AS}. The inherited cable
tree is closed in $\widetilde T$, so it is proper.

The infinite rays are unchanged. Removing vertices outside
$T^\infty$ from a cutset leaves a cutset and cannot increase its
weight; conversely every cutset of $T^\infty$ is one of $T$.
Equality of Green functions proves equality of the infima in
\eqref{eq:DG}. The rays and their finite-segment capacities agree
in both trees, so Proposition~\ref{prop:ray-capacity} proves the
equivalence of \eqref{eq:capacity-condition}.
head: environment

label: eq:energy-cutset-converse
title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~1.1(1) of~\cite{DPR} and
\eqref{eq:capacity-condition} imply that cable Gaussian sign
clusters are bounded. By Lupu's coupling~\cite[Proposition~2.1]{Lupu16},
the same holds for loop clusters at intensity $1/2$. Monotonicity
gives $\widetilde\alpha_{\mathsf c}\ge1/2$, and \eqref{eq:classification} gives $D_G\le1$.
Now \eqref{eq:half-condition} follows from the definition of $D_G$
and \eqref{eq:classification}.

By \eqref{eq:energy-series}, the electrical energy of a unit flow
in the network \eqref{eq:analytic-resistances} is
$\mathcal E_\beta(\mu)-1$. If the cutset condition in
\eqref{eq:half-condition} holds, then $D_G\ge1$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:frostman} gives a finite-energy unit flow for every
$\beta<1$. Conversely, for any unit flow with finite
$\mathcal E_\beta(\mu)$ and any cutset $\Pi$, the pairs of rays
passing through the same $x\in\Pi$ give, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_\beta(\mu)\ge
 \sum_{x\in\Pi}\frac{\mu(x)^2}{\rho_o(x)^\beta}
 \ge\left(\sum_{x\in\Pi}\rho_o(x)^\beta\right)^{-1}.
 \label{eq:energy-cutset-converse}
\end{equation}
Electrical transience is equivalent to existence of a finite-energy
unit flow~\cite[Theorem~2.11]{LP}. This proves the claimed equivalence.

Suppose now that \eqref{eq:analytic-ray-condition} holds on a set
of positive harmonic measure. Fix $0<s<1$ and choose $\eta>0$
with $s(1+\eta/2)\le1$. By \eqref{eq:harmonic-nonatomic}, for
some finite $A\ge1$, the set
\begin{equation}
 B_A=\{\xi:\theta(\xi_n)>0,\quad
       \Lambda(\xi_n)\le A\theta(\xi_n)^{-\eta}
                         \text{ for every }n\ge1\}
 \label{eq:analytic-good-rays}
\end{equation}
has positive harmonic measure. Restrict $\theta$ to $B_A$ and
normalize to obtain a unit flow $\mu$. At every vertex with
$\mu(x)>0$, \eqref{eq:current-factor} implies
\begin{equation}
 \rho_o(x)^s\ge (Ag(o,o))^{-s/2}\theta(x)^{s(1+\eta/2)}
 \ge (Ag(o,o))^{-s/2}\theta(B_A)\mu(x).
 \label{eq:analytic-flow-bound}
\end{equation}
The root cutset has weight one. All other cutsets have weight at
least $(Ag(o,o))^{-s/2}\theta(B_A)>0$ by conservation of $\mu$.
This proves \eqref{eq:half-condition} for every $s<1$.
head: environment

label: prop:degree
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Equation~\eqref{eq:current-factor} gives
$\rho_o(x)\ge c\theta(x)^{1+\kappa/2}$ on the support of
$\theta$, where $c=(Ag(o,o))^{-1/2}$. At
$s=2/(2+\kappa)$, summing over any cutset distinct from $\{o\}$
gives weight at least $c^s\sum_{x\in\Pi}\theta(x)=c^s$.
The root cutset has weight one. This proves the lower bound for
$D_G$; Theorem~\ref{thm:half-analytic} and
\eqref{eq:classification} prove the intensity bounds. For unit
conductances, \eqref{eq:general-current} gives
$\Lambda(x)\le C_x^+\le\deg_T(x)-1$, proving the degree assertion.
head: environment

label: lem:electrical
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:electrical}
Under \eqref{eq:standing}, write $d_x=\deg_T(x)$. For $x\ne o$,
and for adjacent vertices $u,v$, we have
\begin{gather}
 \frac12\le C_{u,v}\le1\qquad(u\sim v),
                                                    \label{eq:branch-conductance}\\
 \frac{d_x-1}{2}\le C_x^+\le d_x-1,\qquad
 \frac12\le a_x\le1,                               \label{eq:C}\\
 \frac{\theta(x)^2}{g(o,o)d_x}\le\rho_o(x)^2
       \le\frac{6\theta(x)^2}{g(o,o)d_x}\quad(x\ne o),\label{eq:current}\\
 \rho(u,v)\le\frac12\quad(u\sim v),\qquad
 \rho_o(x)\le2^{-|x|},\qquad
 \theta(x)\le(2/3)^{|x|}.                            \label{eq:decays}
\end{gather}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each component beyond an oriented edge contains a rooted binary
unit tree, whose conductance is one. In series with the initial
unit edge it has conductance in $[1/2,1]$. This proves
\eqref{eq:branch-conductance}, and summing the appropriate branches
gives \eqref{eq:C}. The ratio $(C_x^++a_x)/(C_x^+)^2$ lies between
$1/d_x$ and $2/(d_x-1)+4/(d_x-1)^2\le6/d_x$.
Equations~\eqref{eq:current-factor} and \eqref{eq:general-current}
therefore give \eqref{eq:current}.
For adjacent $x,y$, the conductance from $x$ through its other
branches is at least one, so $H(x,y)\le1/2$. Equations
\eqref{eq:hitting} and \eqref{eq:multiplicative} give the bounds
on $\rho$. Finally, at least two forward branches share the incoming
current, each with conductance in $[1/2,1]$. No child receives more
than $2/3$ of that current, proving the bound on $\theta$.
head: environment

label: eq:symmetric-exponent
title: Proof
head: environment

label: eq:sparse-branching
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $r\in[0,\infty]$. Set $r_k=r$ when $r<\infty$, and $r_k=k$
when $r=\infty$. We take $b_0=3$ and choose increasing exceptional
generations $n_k\ge1$, with offspring counts
\begin{equation}
 b_n=
 \begin{cases}
  \max\{2,\lceil N_n^{r_k}\rceil\},&n=n_k,\\
  2,&n\ge1\text{ and }n\notin\{n_k:k\ge1\}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:sparse-branching}
\end{equation}
The indices are chosen recursively, starting after generation zero.
Before inserting the $k$th exceptional generation, continue with
binary branching until a new index $n_k$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0\le\frac{\log N_{n_k}}{n_k}-\log2\le\frac1k.
 \label{eq:binary-recovery}
\end{equation}
Such an index exists: if binary branching continues from a fixed
generation $m$, then $N_n=N_m2^{n-m}$ and
$n^{-1}\log N_n\to\log2$. The lower bound in
\eqref{eq:binary-recovery} holds at every generation since
$N_n\ge3\cdot2^{n-1}$. All offspring counts are finite and at least
two, so the tree satisfies \eqref{eq:standing}.

The uniform cylinder flow used in \eqref{eq:spherical-cutsets},
applied to the weights $\lambda^{-n}$, gives
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{br}(T)=\liminf_{n\to\infty}N_n^{1/n}=2,
 \qquad
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log b_n}{\log N_n}=r.
 \label{eq:sparse-branching-exponents}
\end{equation}
Here the branching number is two by
\eqref{eq:binary-recovery}. For the second assertion, the quotient tends to
zero along ordinary generations; at $n_k$ it equals $r_k+o(1)$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:symmetric} now gives
$\widetilde\alpha_{\mathsf c}=(1+r)/(2+r)$, with value one when $r=\infty$.
These values exhaust $[1/2,1]$.

body_md:

Theorem~1.1(2) of~\cite{DPR} gives $\widetilde h_*(T)=0$.

label: lem:GW-capacity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:GW-capacity}
For $\mathbf P_\infty$-almost every tree,
\eqref{eq:ray-capacity-condition}, and hence
\eqref{eq:capacity-condition}, holds.

label: eq:bad-branch-mean
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $W>0$ almost surely, choose $b>0$ so small that, with
$p=\mathbf P_\infty(W<b)$,
\begin{equation}
 a=\bar f'(p)=\mathbf E_\infty[Yp^{Y-1}]<1.
 \label{eq:bad-branch-mean}
\end{equation}
This is possible because $p\downarrow0$ as $b\downarrow0$ and
$\bar f'(p)\to\bar\nu(1)<1$. The derivative is finite for
$p<1$, even when the mean is infinite. At $p=0$ the $Y=1$ term
has value one.

Call a downward step $x\to y$ bad if every other child $z$ of
$x$ has $W_z<b$. Let $N_n$ be the number of length-$n$ paths of
bad steps from the root of an ordinary tree with offspring $Y$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf E_\infty N_n=a^n.
 \label{eq:bad-path-count}
\end{equation}
Conditional on $Y=k$, sum over the first child. The other $k-1$
descendant trees satisfy $W<b$ independently with probability $p$,
and are independent of the path count in the chosen child's tree.
Thus $\mathbf E_\infty N_n=\mathbf E_\infty[Yp^{Y-1}]\mathbf E_\infty N_{n-1}$,
with $N_0=1$. Tonelli's theorem applies without a finite mean.

An infinite path of bad steps would imply $N_n\ge1$ for every
$n$, an event of probability zero by \eqref{eq:bad-path-count}.
Apply this at every nonroot vertex. Every infinite ray
therefore has infinitely many vertices with an off-ray branch
of conductance at least $b$. This proves
\eqref{eq:ray-capacity-condition}; apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:ray-capacity}.

label: lem:terminal
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:terminal-current
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $x$ exists and remove its strict descendants, obtaining a
network $S$. If $S$ is transient, write
$A_x=g_S(o,x)$ and $R_x=g_S(x,x)\ge1$. The latter bound follows
because $x$ is a leaf and its parent edge has resistance one. The
voltage equation at $x$ gives
\begin{equation}
 \theta_T(x)=\frac{A_xC_x^+}{1+R_xC_x^+}
       =U_x\frac{R_xC_x^+}{1+R_xC_x^+},\qquad U_x=\frac{A_x}{R_x}.
 \label{eq:terminal-current}
\end{equation}
Here $U_x$ is the probability of hitting $x$ from $o$ in $S$, so
$U_x\le1$. Since $R_x\ge1$, the last fraction lies between
$C_x^+/(1+C_x^+)=W_x$ and one.

If $S$ is not transient, it consists only of the finite path $[o,x]$:
any side branch would contain an almost surely transient descendant
tree. In this case all the unit current goes through $x$, so set
$U_x=1$. If $x$ does not exist, set $U_x=0$. This proves
\eqref{eq:conditional-flow-comparison} in every case.

Independence of the descendant tree and $\mathcal F_x$ now gives
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E_\infty[\theta_T(x)\mid\mathcal F_x]&\ge\kappa U_x,\nonumber\\
 \mathbf E_\infty[\theta_T(x)\mathbf 1_{\{Y_x\in A\}}\mid\mathcal F_x]
 &\le U_x\mathbf P_\infty(Y\in A)
 \le\kappa^{-1}\mathbf P_\infty(Y\in A)
                 \mathbf E_\infty[\theta_T(x)\mid\mathcal F_x].
 \label{eq:conditional-mark}
\end{align}
Sum over the countable collection of labels at depth $n$ and use
Tonelli's theorem and conservation of flow.

label: eq:degree-tail-on-ray
title: Proof
body_md:
Sample $T$ with law $\mathbf P_\infty$ and then a ray $\xi$ with law
$\theta_T$. Write
$\mathbf Q(dT,d\xi)=\mathbf P_\infty(dT)\theta_T(d\xi)$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:harmonic-domination} gives, for every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Q\{\log\deg_T(\xi_n)>\varepsilon n\}
 \le\kappa^{-1}\mathbf P_\infty\{\log(Y+1)>\varepsilon n\}.
 \label{eq:degree-tail-on-ray}
\end{equation}
The right-hand side is summable by the logarithmic moment
assumption. Borel--Cantelli for positive rational $\varepsilon$
and Fubini's theorem give $\log\deg_T(\xi_n)=o(n)$ on almost every
harmonic ray of almost every tree. By \eqref{eq:harmonic-decay},
$\log(1/\theta_T(\xi_n))\ge cn$ eventually, so
\eqref{eq:ray-assumption} holds. Lemma~\ref{lem:GW-capacity}
verifies the capacity assumption. The degree criterion
\eqref{eq:ray-assumption}, obtained from
Theorem~\ref{thm:half-analytic}, gives the conclusion.

label: prop:truncated-bound
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:retained-flow
title: Proof
body_md:
Such a retained tree survives with positive probability, and its
branching number on survival is $m_M$ by~\cite[Corollary~5.10]{LP}.
For $0<s<\log m_M/\log(M+1)$, \eqref{eq:branching-number}
and max-flow/min-cut give a unit flow $\mu$ on a surviving retained
tree rooted at $v$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \mu(x)\le A(M+1)^{-s|x|_v}
 \label{eq:retained-flow}
\end{equation}
for some finite $A$, where $|x|_v$ is the depth from $v$.

Every retained vertex has degree at most $M+1$ in the ambient
pruned tree $T$.
Writing $H_T$ for hitting probabilities in that tree, for adjacent
retained vertices $x,y$,
\begin{equation}
 \rho_T(x,y)=\sqrt{H_T(x,y)H_T(y,x)}
 \ge\frac1{\sqrt{\deg_T(x)\deg_T(y)}}\ge\frac1{M+1}.
 \label{eq:retained-rho}
\end{equation}
Here the first inequality uses the probability of an immediate step.
Multiplicativity of normalized Green functions along a tree path gives
$\rho_T(v,x)\ge(M+1)^{-|x|_v}$. Consequently
$\mu(x)\le A\rho_T(v,x)^s$. Extend the flow along $[o,v]$ with mass
one and set it to zero on all unused branches. Increasing its constant
over this finite initial path gives $\mu(x)\le A'\rho_o(x)^s$
throughout $T$. Every cutset then has weight at least $1/A'$.

It remains to find a surviving retained tree. Let $a_M>0$ be the
probability of the required event at an ordinary vertex, including
$Y_v\le M$. Under \eqref{eq:leafless-law}, the generation size $L_n$
tends to infinity almost surely. Indeed it is nondecreasing, and a
finite eventual value would require a fixed positive number of
individuals to reproduce with exactly one child forever, an event
of probability zero since $\mathbf P_\infty(Y=1)<1$. Before revealing offspring
at generation $n$, the descendant trees there are independent, so
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf P_\infty(\text{no suitable vertex anywhere})
       \le\mathbf E_\infty(1-a_M)^{L_n}\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:find-subtree}
\end{equation}
The limit follows by bounded convergence. Apply the flow bound and
intersect the resulting events over the countably many eligible $M$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditional on $\mathsf S$, the pruned tree has law $\mathbf P_\infty$
as described in \eqref{eq:surviving-law}. If $Y$ has finite
logarithmic moment, Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-log} gives $D_G=1$.
Otherwise, \eqref{eq:truncated-bound} and
\eqref{eq:truncation-exponent} give $D_G\ge1$, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:GW-capacity} and Theorem~\ref{thm:half-analytic}
give the reverse inequality. Lemma~\ref{lem:pruning} transfers both
$D_G=1$ and \eqref{eq:capacity-condition} to the original tree.
Theorem~\ref{thm:half-analytic} now gives the critical intensity and
non-percolation at one-half. Equations~\eqref{eq:frostman},
\eqref{eq:survival} and \eqref{eq:full-connection} give positive
root percolation probability at every $\alpha>1/2$ on the same
full-probability set of trees.
